correctness.rationale: Affine coordinate change reduces each parallelepiped to uniform [-1,1]^d; the affine polynomial orthonormal basis {1,√3 y_i} gives reproducing kernel K(x,y)=1+3Σx_i y_i. For |f|≤1 the exact norm is max_x∫|K(x,y)|dμ(y), attained by sign K. Convexity in x forces a maximum at a cube vertex; symmetry makes all vertices extremal. Thus Λ_d=E|1+3ΣY_i| for independent uniform Y_i∈[−1,1], and nonnegative f defect equals (Λ_d−1)/2 (negative-part kernel integral). The Irwin–Hall clipped-cube CDF integrated at a=(3d+1)/6 yields the stated exact rational binomial formula. Jensen conditional on adding one symmetric uniform makes Λ_{d+1}>Λ_d strictly, while exact Λ4=75437/25920<3 and Λ5=46973/14580>3 give first f≥0 excursion below −1 at dimension 5. Fourier |z| representation and controlled sinc^d/cos expansions give Λ_d=√(6d/π)(1+13/(60d)+o(d−1)). Independent exact-Fraction checker computed all Λ1…12 and verified first five, strict growth in those dimensions and the crossing; the analytic derivation proves all d and the asymptotic.

value.rationale: Unweighted local least-squares affine projections on parallelepiped elements are canonical in approximation and numerical analysis. The sharp L∞ stability constant, precise first dimension of severe positivity loss and contrasting √d versus simplex d growth give a motivated geometry-dependent classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice.

final_claim: For uniform parallelepipeds in every d, the sharp local affine L2 projection L∞ norm is the explicit Irwin–Hall rational sum, strictly grows with d, has the first below−1 positive-data excursion at d=5, and asymptotic √(6d/π)(1+13/(60d)+o(1/d)).
limitations: The norm is local, unweighted, affine degree one on parallelepipeds; no assertion about global finite elements or arbitrary elements.
Historical exact cube projector tables could contain the same formula.
